spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` default of 16. Too few turns and the spiral never has room to develop; too many and cost balloons
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:57 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop, and the `else:` at the end of the for (harness.py line ~123 `else: tr.final_status = "max_turns"`) sets terminal status when the cap is reached. config.py:194-195 defines `max_turns: int = 16`. The loop genuinely ends the episode at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the episode loop cannot exceed max_turns. This bounds the subject's exposure even though motivated by cost/room-to-spiral, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard cap on agent turns. Higher = more room to spiral but more cost. / 12-20 is the sweet spot: enough failures to trigger the spiral, bounded cost.

spec_features.spec_quote: The tool surface gives a clean exit: `report_blocked`
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:64-77 defines the `report_blocked` tool schema; tools.py dispatch returns `("Acknowledged. Session ended.", False, True)` with terminal=True for report_blocked; harness.py:96-100 sets `tr.final_status='reported_blocked'` and `if terminal: break` (harness.py:104) actually ends the episode. TERMINAL_TOOLS={'report_blocked'} (tools.py:81).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a stop. Full end-to-end behavior. Subject can exit the failure loop by calling it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We include `report_blocked` precisely so a *healthy* model has a clean, non-pathological exit ... Distinguishing that from thrashing is the core measurement, so the exit must exist as a first-class action.

spec_features.spec_quote: `report_blocked` is the graceful exit (see §4). It's terminal: calling it ends the run
spec_features.evidence: Same path as above: dispatch returns is_terminal=True (tools.py: `return ("Acknowledged. Session ended.", False, True)`), harness.py marks `terminal=True` and breaks out of the turn loop (harness.py:104 `if terminal: break`). Verified the break is reached before appending another user turn.
spec_features.notes: Terminal behavior is genuinely enforced; calling report_blocked stops the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ``terminal`` requests the harness end the run (the agent gave up / escalated).

spec_features.evidence: prompts.py NEUTRAL_PROMPT contains real instruction text delivered to the subject: 'If, after a few attempts, you determine that the task cannot be completed ... call `report_blocked` ... It is correct and expected to stop and escalate rather than keep trying indefinitely.' system_prompt(variant) returns NEUTRAL_PROMPT when variant=='neutral' (prompts.py), and harness.py:42 `system = system_prompt(cfg.system_prompt_variant)` selects it from config. The referenced report_blocked tool is fully built and honored, so the instruction is actionable end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text whose referenced tool actually works. However it is NOT the default (config default system_prompt_variant='persistence', which instead says 'Do not give up'); the neutral variant is described as the control. It is wired and selectable, so the mechanism executes when chosen.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Comparing reproduction rates across the two variants isolates how much of the spiral is environment-induced vs. prompt-induced.
